title: Fit and Proper for Firms: Appointing and Assessing Key Function Holders
summary: A nine-module programme showing firms how to appoint and assess key function holders, prepare applications and interviews, and manage fitness and certification on an ongoing basis.
intro: This training programme equips firms to appoint and assess directors and key function holders who meet the fit and proper standard, from role design and candidate due diligence to applications, regulatory interviews and annual certification.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give the people who run a firm's appointments process a complete, operational method for assessing fitness and propriety, taught by former regulators who show how the authority tests the firm's work. Participants leave able to run defensible due diligence, submit applications that succeed first time, prepare candidates for interview and manage fitness on an ongoing basis.
sections.What It Covers: The fit and proper standard and the firm's obligations, role design and succession, integrity and reputation checks, competence, capability and capacity, controllers and change in control, applications to the authority, preparing candidates for regulatory interviews, ongoing fitness and annual certification, and handling adverse information.
Intended Audience: Heads of compliance, company secretaries and governance teams who manage approved and certified roles
HR, talent and nominations committee support staff responsible for senior appointments and references
Senior managers and chairs who sponsor appointments and sign off fitness assessments
Learning Objectives: Explain the components of the fit and proper standard and the firm's primary responsibility for meeting it
Design role profiles and succession plans that define what fitness means for each key function
Apply proportionate due diligence on integrity, reputation, competence and capacity, and document the judgement
Prepare complete and consistent applications to the authority, including for owners and controllers
Prepare candidates for regulatory interviews so they demonstrate understanding rather than recitation
Manage ongoing fitness, annual certification and adverse information fairly and in line with notification duties
sections.Structure and Format: Nine modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines practical tools with case studies, exercises and mock interviews, and modules can be selected or tailored to the firm's roles and accountability regime.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of compliance, company secretarial, HR or governance work in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior experience of regulatory applications is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)

modules.title: The Fit and Proper Standard: What the Firm Must Show
modules.summary: The components of the fit and proper test, which roles fall within it, and why the authority expects the firm, not the regulator, to be the first and most rigorous assessor.
objectives: Explain honesty, integrity, competence, capability and financial soundness as applied by authorities
Identify the roles that require pre-approval, certification or notification
Explain the firm's primary responsibility and the consequences of weak assessments
syllabus: Components of the test and international standards from IOSCO, the Basel Committee and FATF
Pre-approved, certified and notified roles under accountability regimes
Proportionality by firm size, role and business model
Regulatory findings and enforcement cases on poor appointment practice

modules.title: Role Design, Role Profiles and Succession
modules.summary: How to define each key function so fitness can be assessed against it, how individual roles combine into a collectively suitable board and management team, and how to plan succession.
objectives: Design role profiles that state responsibilities, competencies and time commitment
Assess collective suitability across the board and senior team
Plan succession and interim cover for key functions
syllabus: Role profiles, statements of responsibilities and responsibilities maps
Competency frameworks for risk, compliance, MLRO, finance and executive roles
Skills matrices, independence and collective suitability
Succession pipelines, interim appointments and handovers

modules.title: Due Diligence: Honesty, Integrity and Reputation
modules.summary: The checks a firm should complete before appointment, how to obtain and use regulatory references, and how to weigh past conduct, disclosures and non-disclosure.
objectives: Design a proportionate pre-appointment checking process
Obtain and interpret regulatory references and previous employer information
Weigh past conduct by seriousness, recency, pattern and rehabilitation
syllabus: Criminal, regulatory, civil, insolvency and directorship checks
Regulatory references, open-source research and media checks
Weighing past conduct and non-financial misconduct
Non-disclosure as a fitness issue in its own right

modules.title: Competence, Capability and Capacity
modules.summary: How to test whether a candidate has the knowledge, experience and time the role requires, using evidence rather than assertion, and how to close gaps without lowering the standard.
objectives: Assess competence against the role profile using documentary and interview evidence
Judge capacity, other commitments and conflicts of interest
Design development plans and conditions where gaps exist
syllabus: Evidence of experience, qualifications and track record
Structured competency interviews and scenario questions
Time commitment, multiple directorships and conflicts of interest
Closing gaps: induction, development plans and conditional appointments

modules.title: Owners, Controllers and Change in Control
modules.summary: How the firm supports applications by proposed owners and controllers, maps its ownership chain, and evidences source of wealth and source of funds to the authority's satisfaction.
objectives: Map ownership chains and identify controllers and beneficial owners
Prepare controllers for the authority's assessment of reputation and financial soundness
Evidence source of wealth and source of funds credibly
syllabus: Control thresholds, acting in concert and indirect holdings
Mapping ownership and beneficial ownership for the authority
Source of wealth narratives and supporting documents
Red flags the authority looks for: nominees, layered structures and secrecy

modules.title: Applications to the Authority
modules.summary: How to prepare and manage fit and proper applications so they are complete, consistent and timely, and how to handle questions, delays and the risk of withdrawal or refusal.
objectives: Prepare applications that are complete, consistent and fully disclosed
Manage timetables, interim arrangements and questions from the authority
Recognise why applications stall, are withdrawn or are refused
syllabus: Application content, disclosures and consistency with the business plan
Timing, interim arrangements and acting before approval
Answering the authority's questions: evidence, tone and avoiding new issues
Conditions, minded-to-refuse processes, withdrawals and representations

modules.title: Preparing Candidates for Regulatory Interviews
modules.summary: How authorities plan and run competence interviews, what they are really testing, and how the firm prepares candidates through briefing and mock interviews without scripting them.
objectives: Explain how authority interviewers prepare and what they test by role
Prepare candidates on the firm's risks, controls and their own accountabilities
Run mock interviews that build genuine understanding rather than recitation
syllabus: The interview file: how authorities build questions from the application
Role-specific scenarios for chief executive, chair, compliance, risk and MLRO
Common failures: generic answers, deferring to others and over-rehearsal
Role-play: mock interview of a proposed head of compliance

modules.title: Ongoing Fitness and Annual Certification
modules.summary: How to keep fitness under review after appointment, run annual certification and assessments efficiently, and link fitness to performance, conduct breaches and remuneration.
objectives: Design an annual fitness and certification process with clear evidence
Identify triggers for reassessment during the year
Link conduct breaches, performance and training records to fitness
syllabus: Annual self-declarations, checks and certification sign-off
Triggers for reassessment: role changes, incidents and new information
Conduct rules breaches, training records and remuneration adjustments
Record-keeping and evidencing assessments to the supervisor

modules.title: Adverse Information, Removal and Case Workshop
modules.summary: How to respond fairly when adverse information emerges, including investigation, notification to the authority, conditions and removal, followed by a workshop working two cases to decision.
objectives: Respond to adverse information with a fair and timely process
Decide on notification, conditions, suspension or removal
Apply the programme to realistic appointment and reassessment cases
syllabus: Investigating adverse information fairly and promptly
Notification duties, regulatory references on departure and settlement agreements
Conditions, suspension, removal and the risk of prohibition
Workshop: a director appointment and a mid-year reassessment to decision

related.title: Engaging Effectively with Your Supervisor: How Firms Are Assessed
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how supervisors assess business models, governance and risk, so they can see themselves as the supervisor does and engage with confidence.

related.title: Governance Reviews and Supervisory Interviews: Preparing Your Board and Management
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors assess governance and interview directors and staff, and how licensees can evidence effective governance and prepare openly.

related.title: Recovery and Wind-Down Planning for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms build credible recovery and wind-down plans, from scenarios and triggers to client asset return, testing and supervisory review.

related.title: Regulatory Investigations and Enforcement: Responding as a Firm
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how to prepare for, manage and respond to supervisory investigations and enforcement, from first information request to settlement.

related.title: Regulatory Readiness: Authorisation and Supervisory Engagement
related.summary: A ten-module programme taking firms from licence application through to established supervision, showing how authorities assess applications and supervise new firms.

related.title: Supervisory Findings and Remediation: From Risk Assessment to Closure
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors reach findings and how licensees can respond with remediation that fixes root causes and closes issues on evidence.
